title: Protocol for bevacizumab purification using Ac-PHQGQHIGVSK-agarose
author: Barredo, Giudicessi, et al.
materials: Material•Absorption UV/VIS spectrophotometer•10 mm silica UV cell

Material•Absorption UV/VIS spectrophotometer•10 mm silica UV cell•Orbital shaker•20 mM sodium phosphate, 1 M (NH4)2SO4, pH 7.0•Labeled conical centrifuge micro tubes•Labeled polypropylene columns fitted with a polyethylene porous disk.•Pure bevacizumab solutions of known concentration•Bradford reagent•Thermomixer (Eppendorf)•Sigma Plot software (http://www.sigmaplot.com/products/sigmaplot/sigmaplot-details.php)

steps.title: Synthesize peptide Ac-PHQGQHIGVSK-NH2
steps.instruction: Perform solid‑phase Fmoc synthesis of Ac‑PHQGQHIGVSK‑NH2 in a polypropylene column with a polyethylene porous disk inside a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Place 1 g Rink‑Amide‑MBHA resin (0.67 meq g⁻¹) in the solid‑phase reactor (this amount yields ~0.5 mmol peptide assuming 75 % overall yield; crude purity >90 % is acceptable).
Wash resin three times with CH₂Cl₂, then with DMF.
Deprotect Fmoc by incubating resin with 20 % piperidine in DMF (v/v) for 2 × 5 min.
Wash resin with DMF 5 × 1 min.
For each coupling cycle, weigh Fmoc‑Lys(Boc)‑OH (3 eq) and TBTU (3 eq), dissolve in minimal DMF, add to resin, then add DIEA (4 eq) dropwise and mix.
Agitate resin on an orbital shaker for 45 min at room temperature.
Wash resin with DMF (2 × 1 mL) and CH₂Cl₂ (2 × 1 mL) by filtration or decantation.

Test 1–3 mg of resin with the Kaiser test; if positive, repeat the coupling steps (weigh reagents, add, DIEA, 45 min, wash, test) until negative, then proceed to the next Fmoc‑protected amino acid using steps 3–9.
After completing the peptide chain, acetylate the terminal proline by adding Ac₂O (10 eq) and DIC (10 eq) in enough CH₂Cl₂ to just mobilize the swollen resin.
Incubate 1 h at room temperature.
Confirm acetylation with the chloranil test on 1–3 mg resin.
Cleave peptide and remove side‑chain protecting groups by treating resin with 15 mL TFA/TIS/H₂O/DODT (92 : 5.2 : 2.5 : 2.5) for 2 h.
Filter to remove resin; add the filtrate to 10‑fold volume cold ethyl ether to precipitate peptide.
Centrifuge 2000–3000 × g at 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with additional cold diethyl ether and centrifuge again under the same conditions.
Dissolve the washed peptide in MeCN/H₂O (1 : 1) and lyophilize to obtain dry Ac‑PHQGQHIGVSK‑NH2.

steps.title: Couple peptide to NHS‑agarose
steps.instruction: Immobilize the synthesized peptide on dry NHS‑activated agarose to generate the affinity matrix.

substeps.instruction: Place 150 mg dry NHS‑activated agarose (≈1 mL hydrated resin) in a polypropylene column fitted with a polyethylene porous disk.
Wash the resin with pure DMSO three times, each wash lasting 5 min.
Dissolve 50 mg peptide Ac‑PHQGQHIGVSK‑NH2 in 1 mL DMSO and add the solution to the washed agarose (the peptide amount is ~2‑fold excess over NHS groups).
Add anhydrous triethylamine in a molar amount equal to the peptide amount, gently shake the slurry for 2 h at room temperature.
Filter the reaction mixture and retain the filtrate for later analysis.
Wash the gel three times with DMSO.
Block any remaining activated NHS groups by adding 50 µL ethanolamine dissolved in 450 µL DMSO; incubate 30 min at room temperature.
Wash the matrix sequentially with: DMSO; DMSO/H₂O (70 : 30); DMSO/H₂O (50 : 50); DMSO/H₂O (30 : 70); and finally with degassed deionized water.

steps.title: Assess peptide immobilization
steps.instruction: Quantify the amount of peptide coupled to agarose by measuring released NHS in the saved filtrate.

substeps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of the filtrate (saved in step 2, item 5) at 260 nm using a UV/VIS spectrophotometer with a 10 mm silica cell.
Calculate the NHS concentration using the molar extinction coefficient ε = 9600 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹ at 260 nm.

steps.title: Determine adsorption isotherms
steps.instruction: Measure bevacizumab binding to the peptide‑agarose in batch experiments to obtain isotherm parameters.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate the Ac‑PHQGQHIGVSK‑agarose with 20 column volumes of adsorption buffer (20 mM sodium phosphate, 1 M (NH₄)₂SO₄, pH 7.0).

Prepare a 1 : 1 suspension of the equilibrated matrix in the same buffer; using a cut‑tip pipette, transfer 100 µL of this suspension to each labeled 1.5 mL conical centrifuge tube, which delivers 50 µL of matrix per tube.
To each tube add increasing volumes of pure bevacizumab stock solution and buffer so that the final volume is exactly 1 mL.
Prepare a parallel set of control tubes containing the same volumes of bevacizumab stock and buffer but **without** matrix.
Place all tubes on an orbital shaker inside a Thermomixer and incubate overnight (~16 h) at 25 °C to reach equilibrium.
Separate resin from each tube by filtration using labeled polypropylene columns with porous disks.
Determine the protein concentration in each filtrate with the Bradford reagent.
Calculate the free equilibrium concentration (c*) from the matrix‑containing tubes and the initial total concentration (c_t) from the control tubes.
Compute the bound amount per matrix volume: q* = (c_t − c*) × 1000 / 509.
Fit the q* versus c* data to the Langmuir equation q* = q_m c*/(K_d + c*) using SigmaPlot (one‑site model) to obtain the maximum capacity q_m and dissociation constant K_d.

steps.title: Purify bevacizumab from CHO culture
steps.instruction: Apply the peptide‑agarose column to clarified CHO cell supernatant and recover bevacizumab under mild conditions.

substeps.instruction: Clarify the CHO cell culture containing bevacizumab by centrifugation or filtration.
Add solid (NH₄)₂SO₄ to the clarified supernatant to reach a final concentration of 1 M.
Equilibrate a chromatography column packed with 0.5 mL (0.5 × 2.5 cm) Ac‑PHQGQHIGVSK‑agarose with 20 column volumes of adsorption buffer (20 mM sodium phosphate, pH 7.0, 1 M (NH₄)₂SO₄).
Load the column with the prepared CHO filtrate (ensure the amount of bevacizumab does not exceed the matrix capacity determined in step 4).
Wash the column with adsorption buffer until the UV absorbance at 280 nm of the effluent returns to baseline.
Elute bound bevacizumab by applying 20 mM sodium phosphate, pH 7.0 (no salt).
Measure the total protein concentration of the eluate with the Bradford assay, using pure bevacizumab as the standard.
Determine the bevacizumab concentration by HPLC on a protein A analytical column as described by Zou et al.
Analyze the purified fractions by SDS‑PAGE (12.5 % gel, reductive conditions) and stain with Coomassie Blue following standard protocols.
